name: Jeroboam
overview: Jeroboam was a male king of Israel, noted specifically as the son of Joash (Jehoash). His reign and lineage are documented in the books of 2 Kings, highlighting his role in the history of Israel's monarchy. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him in the provided data.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroboam means 'the people increase,' reflecting a Hebrew meaning that may indicate a role connected to the growth or leadership of the people. Additionally, he held the title 'King of Israel,' which straightforwardly identifies his royal position over the northern kingdom.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeroboam as the son of Joash (Jehoash). It is also inferred that Zechariah was his father, suggesting a generational lineage. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are detailed in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroboam's significance in Scripture centers on his kingship over Israel, marking him as a key figure in the continuation of the northern kingdom's monarchy. His identification as the son of Joash situates him within the royal lineage, underscoring the dynastic succession. His name's meaning and royal title emphasize his leadership and the growth of Israel under his reign.
